scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

But here's the thing: I'm the only one in a group of eight who isn't in the Honors College at our school. People, including my friends, have told me that this doesn't mean they're smarter or harder working than me, and I've tried to accept that. However, being in the Honors College means they have some required courses that I don't, so they all have classes together without me. When we hang out, they often talk about their classes, and I feel completely left out. Now, I found out that next year, they're all moving into the Honors College dorm building together. I can't live there since I'm not in the Honors College, and I already feel left out enough. With them living together, it seems even more likely that they'll end up hanging out without me because they'll be around each other all the time. I tried talking to a couple of them about it, and one person said I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together. I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they'd realize that seven people of an eight-person group living together is rather unfair. I don't want to have to start over and find new friends, but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. Is it AITA (Ask a Internet Therapist/Advisor) to feel this way? I'm feeling excluded, and that's making me question whether I should try to keep these friendships or find new ones. I also feel like my friends aren't considering my feelings when they're making plans or talking about things that I can't be part of. That makes me feel like they're not empathetic towards me. But is that a fair assessment? Maybe they're just excited about their new living situation and don't realize how it's affecting me. On the other hand, I don't want to lose these friends because they mean a lot to me, especially since I'm shy and making new friends is hard for me. But I also don't want to be in a situation where I'm constantly feeling excluded and left out. I guess I need to figure out whether it's reasonable to expect my friends to make an effort to include me, even if they're living together and have different schedules. Is it too much to ask for them to consider my feelings and make an effort to maintain our friendship? Or is it understandable that they might drift apart because of these changes? I also need to consider whether I'm being too sensitive or if my feelings are justified. It's tough because I don't want to come off as entitled, but I also don't want to be the one who's always feeling left out. Maybe I should think about how I can communicate my feelings more effectively without making my friends feel guilty or defensive. It's a delicate balance because I don't want to push them away, but I also need them to understand how I'm feeling. I wonder if there are ways to maintain the friendship despite the changes. Maybe we can set up regular hangouts outside of their living situation or find activities that we can all enjoy together. However, if they're unwilling to make that effort, then maybe it's time to consider finding new friends who are more aligned with my circumstances. In the end, I need to decide whether it's worth fighting for these friendships or if it's healthier to move on and find a new group that better fits my situation.
